Authors: Calabrese C, Reale M, Dallari V, Trecca EMC, Giuntoli DG, Caivano F, Visconti IC, Battilocchi L, Bulfamante AM
Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10823-7
Published: 2026-Nov-14
PMID: 43026353



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Pediatric benign vocal fold lesions (BVFLs) are a common cause of chronic dysphonia in children, yet evidence on their diagnosis and management remains heterogeneous and unsystematized. This review aims to critically synthesize the available evidence on diagnostic strategies, comparative treatment outcomes, and indications for surgical management of BVFLs in the pediatric population. METHODS: This PRISMA-compliant systematic review searched PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science for studies published between January 2000 and March 2026. Eligible studies included patients aged ≤ 18 years with endoscopically confirmed BVFLs and reported diagnostic or treatment outcomes. Study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and findings were synthesized descriptively with Wilson 95% confidence intervals. RESULTS: Ten studies including 559 children were analyzed. Vocal fold nodules accounted for 86.7% of lesions, and flexible laryngoscopy was the most commonly used diagnostic tool. Conservative management was used in 88.0% of patients, with improvement rates of 75.5%-87.5% and no reported complications. Surgery was performed in 12.0%, with improvement rates of 79.2%-100%; one study reported postoperative complications in 20% of patients. Surgical indications were not standardized, and median follow-up was 4.5 months. CONCLUSION: Conservative management, primarily behavioral voice therapy, is safe, effective, and should remain the first-line treatment for pediatric BVFLs. Surgery is an appropriate secondary option for structural or refractory lesions, but requires stringent patient selection given the risk of permanent vocal fold damage. Evidence gaps in standardized surgical indications, outcome measures, and long-term follow-up represent priorities for future prospective multicenter research.

Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10817-5
Published: 2026-Nov-14
PMID: 43026352



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The superior turbinate and sphenoid ostium are commonly used landmarks for sphenoidotomy; however, they may be obscured in severe inflammatory conditions such as eosinophilic chronic rhinosinusitis (ECRS) or affected by anatomical variations. This study evaluated the orbito-pterygo-sphenoidal ligament/posterior septal artery (OPSL/PSA) complex-guided transethmoidal sphenoidotomy (TES) as an anatomy-based approach for sphenoid sinus entry and controlled inferior extension of anterior sphenoid wall (ASW) removal. METHODS: This retrospective study included patients with ECRS who underwent sphenoidotomy. Outcomes were compared between the OPSL/PSA complex-guided TES group (24 patients, 48 sides) and a conventional group (25 patients, 50 sides). The primary endpoint was postoperative residual inferior ASW height measured using computed tomography. Secondary endpoints included ASW width, intraoperative events, operative time, and postoperative exploratory outcomes. RESULTS: Postoperative residual inferior ASW height was significantly smaller in the OPSL/PSA complex-guided TES group than in the conventional group (-0.8 ± 1.8 vs. 1.5 ± 2.5 mm; p < 0.001). The difference remained significant after adjustment for potential confounders. Superior turbinate resection was not performed in the OPSL/PSA complex-guided TES group, whereas it was performed in 28.0% of sides in the conventional group. No statistically significant differences in operative time or PSA-related hemorrhage were observed between groups. CONCLUSIONS: The OPSL/PSA complex-guided TES was associated with a greater extent of inferior ASW removal and less frequent superior turbinate resection, with no statistically significant differences in operative time or ​PSA-related hemorrhage between groups. The OPSL/PSA complex may serve as a complementary anatomical reference with a dual function: assisting sphenoid sinus entry and guiding controlled inferior ASW removal in patients with ECRS.

Authors: Pawlica MT, Filipowicz J, Gabrysz Z, Cackowski MM, Grabczan W, Blachnio A, Orlowski TM
Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10814-8
Published: 2026-Nov-14
PMID: 43026346



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Laser thermal ablation (LTA) is a minimally invasive treatment for thyroid nodules with a generally favorable safety profile. We report the first case of tracheoesophageal fistula (TEF) following LTA, which is a life-threatening complication requiring urgent multidisciplinary management. METHODS: A 71-year-old woman with a history of breast cancer, nodular goiter, and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) underwent LTA for a benign thyroid nodule (Bethesda II). Clinical data, imaging, endoscopic findings, surgical management, and postoperative course are described. RESULTS: Immediately post-procedure, the patient experienced dysphagia, dyspnea, and pain. Two days later, the patient was hospitalized due to thyroiditis, which was managed with corticosteroids. Twelve days later, she was readmitted due to gastrointestinal bleeding and anemia. Bronchoscopy, gastroscopy, and computed tomography revealed a 30 mm necrotic defect with TEF and right vocal cord paralysis. The patient was referred to our institution with intent to prehabilitate and surgically repair the defect. However, due to massive hemoptysis and airway obstruction caused by the goiter, a life-saving tracheostomy and total right hemithyroidectomy were performed. The defect was repaired with esophageal and tracheal suturing, reinforced with a sternocleidomastoid (SCM) muscle flap. On postoperative day 10, a 6 mm fistula recurrence was diagnosed, necessitating successful surgical revision. The patient was discharged in good condition. CONCLUSION: This case highlights a devastating complication following a minimally invasive procedure. While major complications of LTA are rare, clinicians must remain vigilant regarding preoperative risk factors, particularly large substernal goiters, and post-procedural red flags. Surgical intervention remains the gold standard for the management of acquired TEF.

Authors: Domínguez-Rodríguez S, Tagarro A, Moraleda C, Buck WC, Mujuru H, Chabala C, Mvalo T, Iroh-Tam PY, Cossa A, Madrid L, et al.
Journal: Lancet (London, England) | DOI: 10.1016/S0140-6736(26)01418-2
Published: 2026-Nov-14
PMID: 43020097



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mortality among infants with severe HIV-associated pneumonia remains high globally. The EMPIRICAL trial evaluated whether empirical tuberculosis treatment (eTB-T) improves survival compared with the currently recommended microbiologically and clinically guided strategy. METHODS: This multicentre, open-label, group-sequential designed, 2×2 factorial, randomised, controlled, superiority trial was conducted in 19 hospitals across Côte d'Ivoire, Malawi, Mozambique, Uganda, Zambia, and Zimbabwe. Infants aged 28-365 days admitted with severe HIV-associated pneumonia, without a current tuberculosis diagnosis or contact, were centrally and individually randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) using a secure web-based system stratified by site and severity. A computer-generated block randomisation schedule was used, with fixed blocks of eight allocations (two allocations to each factorial treatment group) within each stratum. Participants received standard of care (SoC) comprising treatment for bacterial (WHO-recommended antibiotics) and Pneumocystis jirovecii (cotrimoxazole and steroids) pneumonia, SoC plus 15 days of oral valganciclovir (16 mg/kg per 12 h), or SoC plus 6 months of tuberculosis treatment (isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol for 2 months, plus isoniazid and rifampicin for 4 subsequent months), or both interventions combined. Here, we report the comparison between the eTB-T (ie, SoC plus tuberculosis treatment and SoC plus oral valganciclovir plus tuberculosis treatment) and non-eTB-T (ie, SoC or SoC plus 15 days of oral valganciclovir) groups. Nasopharyngeal aspirates, stools for Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra testing, and urine for tuberculosis lipoarabinomannan assay were collected at recruitment. In the non-eTB-T groups, tuberculosis treatment was initiated if microbiological results collected at recruitment yielded positive results or if, during follow-up, the treating clinician suspected tuberculosis on clinical grounds, including radiological findings, in accordance with routine clinical practice and guidelines. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality (at 15 days and 360 days). Survival was estimated using flexible parametric models with covariate-adjusted conditional estimates; missing data were imputed by chained equations. The trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03915366) and is now complete. FINDINGS: Between March 15, 2020, and Jan 31, 2024, 563 participants were enrolled; 558 were analysed after excluding five patients who did not meet eligibility criteria. 276 participants were allocated to the eTB-T groups (n=140 eTB-T and n=136 valganciclovir plus eTB-T) and 282 to the non-eTB-T groups (n=142 SoC and n=140 valganciclovir). 17 (6%) of 276 in the eTB-T groups and 20 (7%) of 282 in the non-eTB-T groups were lost to follow-up. Median age was 4·4 months (IQR 3·2-7·4) and 274 (49%) of participants were female and 284 (51%) were male. In the non-eTB-T groups, 130 (46%) of 282 participants eventually initiated tuberculosis treatment at a median of 4·0 days (IQR 3·0-15·0) after recruitment due to positive microbiological findings in 55 (20%) cases (53 confirmed by tuberculosis lipoarabinomannan assay and two by nasopharyngeal aspirates Xpert MTB/RIF) or clinical decision in 75 (27%) cases. There was no evidence of interaction between valganciclovir and eTB-T (adjusted hazard ratio 1·19, 95% CI 0·73-1·95; pheterogeneity=0·4836). At 12 months, 132 (48%) of 276 participants in eTB-T groups and 121 (43%) of 282 participants in non-eTB-T groups died. In the eTB-T groups, the adjusted hazard ratio for death was 1·12 (95% CI 0·87-1·43; p=0·3868). At 15 days, the odds ratio was 1·24 (95% CI 0·83-1·84; p=0·2950). Serious adverse events did not differ between groups (1·19, 0·82-1·73; p=0·3523). There were no treatment-related deaths. The most common adverse events were elevation of transaminases (72 [26%] cases in the eTB-T groups and 74 [26%] in the non-eTB-T group), anaemia (163 [59%] cases in the eTB-T groups and 169 [60%] in the non-eTB-T groups), and infectious disease requiring antimicrobial treatment (161 [58%] cases in the eTB-T groups and 176 [62%] in the non-eTB-T groups). INTERPRETATION: In contrast to empirical treatment with valganciclovir, there was no evidence that eTB-T was superior to a clinically and microbiologically guided strategy in reducing all-cause mortality among infants with HIV-associated pneumonia. However, the high proportion of infants who eventually initiated tuberculosis treatment during follow-up in the non-eTB-T groups might have reduced the contrast between strategies and attenuated the ability to detect differences in outcomes. FUNDING: European and Developing Countries Clinical Trials Partnership.

Authors: McHugh N, Bawa J, Qureishi A, Martinez-Devesa P, Jeyaretna S, Boukas A, Silva P, Gupta KK, Mughal Z
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.71054
Published: 2026-Nov-13
PMID: 43025857



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Sinonasal inverted papilloma (IP) is a benign epithelial neoplasm with a propensity for malignant transformation. Reported rates of synchronous or metachronous carcinoma vary widely. Our aim was to determine the rates of both synchronous and metachronous malignancy in patients with IP. DATA SOURCES: Embase, MEDLINE, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library were searched from 2005 until June 2026. REVIEW METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. Prevalences were pooled using a random-effects model. RESULTS: A total of 68 studies (n = 7412 patients) were identified. The pooled prevalence of overall malignancy was 5.6% (95% CI: 4.5-6.8), comprising synchronous malignancy in 4.3% (95% CI: 3.4-5.3), and metachronous malignancy in 1.3% (95% CI: 0.8-2.0). The pooled recurrence rate was 17.5% (95% CI: 15.0-20.2). CONCLUSIONS: These weighted, IP-specific estimates place the prevalence of malignancy in inverted papilloma below the figures most often cited in the literature. These findings provide a methodologically robust benchmark for patient counseling and postoperative surveillance.

Authors: Jiménez-Labaig P, Sanz-Beltran J, Forster MD, Bossi P, Metcalf R, Garcia IB, Hanna GJ, Cabezas-Camarero S, Harrington KJ
Journal: Oral oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oraloncology.2026.108228
Published: 2026-Nov-13
PMID: 43025371



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Salivary gland cancers (SGCs) are rare and heterogeneous tumors lacking standard systemic treatment options in the recurrent/metastatic setting. Although clinical trials have shown activity of anti-HER2, chemotherapy, androgen receptor-targeted agents (ARTA) and androgen deprivation therapies (ADT), their combined effects remain largely unexplored. We aimed to model the potential outcomes of rational drug combinations to guide future clinical trial designs. METHODS: Fifteen phase II trials were included, encompassing 524 patients (19% female, 81% R/M, 55% ductal, 11% adenocarcinoma, 5% mucoepidermoid). 7 trials assessed cytotoxic chemotherapy, 6 ARTA ± ADT, and 5 anti-HER2 therapies (3 as antibody-drug conjugates, ADCs). Overall response rate (ORR) and grade ≥ 3 treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) were estimated using Bliss and additivity models. Median progression-free survival and overall survival (OS) were reconstructed using parametric survival models. RESULTS: Sixty combinations were assessed. In AR + HER2 + disease, triple combinations involving ARTA-ADT and anti-HER2-ADCs, or chemotherapy plus anti-HER2 yielded the highest predicted ORRs (94.5% by Bliss). In AR + HER2-, chemotherapy-based combinations and ARTA-ADT showed a greater relative ORR gain overall compared with AR + HER2+: +14.29(1.1-21.9) vs + 6.26(0.8-14.3). Estimated median 5- and 3-year OS was achieved in AR + HER2 + and AR + HER2- combinations respectively. Grade ≥ 3 TRAEs showed the highest rates in chemotherapy regimens (93.1 by Bliss, uncapped 126.5% by additivity) and lower toxicity with ADCs (23.3%, 24.8%). CONCLUSIONS: Predicted efficacy and safety outcomes highlight potential rational drug combinations that merit evaluation in future SGC clinical trials, ideally using a sequential approach, with particularly promising incremental benefit in AR + HER2- disease. Expected toxicity may constrain the feasibility of certain combination strategies.

Authors: Juma J, Luoma J, Traore A, Sangare A, Bouare O, Cheick Haidara F, Samaké O, Adubra L, Ihamuotila R, Martell O, et al.
Journal: PLoS medicine | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pmed.1005296
Published: 2026-Nov-13
PMID: 43024632



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mass azithromycin administration has been used to reduce under-five mortality in sub-Saharan Africa, but concerns remain about its potential impact on antimicrobial resistance (AMR). METHODS AND FINDINGS: The Large-scale Assessment of the Key health-promoting Activities of two New mass drug administration regiments with Azithromycin (LAKANA) trial was a cluster-randomized, placebo-controlled trial conducted in Mali, enrolling infants aged 1-11 months randomized to placebo, twice-yearly azithromycin, or quarterly azithromycin for 2 years. The trial did not find any mortality benefit amongst treated children. The current analysis is a sub-study of the parent trial examining AMR outcomes. Repeated cross-sectional nasopharyngeal and rectal swabs were collected from children aged 4-14-months in villages randomized to placebo, twice-yearly or quarterly azithromycin, and from untreated contacts aged 49-59-months at baseline, 12-, 24-, and 36-months post-village enrollment across 59 LAKANA trial villages. Phenotypic resistance to macrolide and nonmacrolide antibiotics was assessed in Streptococcus pneumoniae (S. pneumoniae) and Escherichia coli (E. coli) isolates using disk diffusion or E-tests. The primary noninferiority analysis evaluated macrolide resistance prevalence at 36-months among younger children and at 24-months among older contacts, with predefined margin of +10 percentage points. A total of 5,025 nasopharyngeal and 5,021 rectal samples were analyzed. At baseline, among 4-14-month-old children, macrolide resistance in S. pneumoniae was 16.6%, 15.5%, and 11.1% in the placebo, twice-yearly and quarterly azithromycin groups, respectively, and 5.0%, 5.0%, and 0.0% in E. coli. At 36-months, corresponding prevalences were 13.4%, 14.5%, and 17.2% for S. pneumoniae, and 5.1%, 6.4%, and 9.1% for E. coli. The difference between placebo and twice-yearly groups was 1.0% (95% CI [-4.7, 6.8]) for S. pneumoniae and 1.3% (95% CI [-2.4, 4.9]) for E. coli; corresponding differences for quarterly azithromycin group was 3.8% (95% CI [-3.3, 10.9]) for S. pneumoniae and 4.0% (95% CI [-0.7, 8.7]) for E. coli. Among untreated older children, there were no marked inter-group differences in macrolide resistance either at baseline or at 24-months. The study may not have been large enough to detect a small increase in macrolide resistance in S. pneumoniae among young children in villages that received quarterly azithromycin. CONCLUSIONS: Twice-yearly azithromycin administration to 1-11-month-old infants for 2 years in Mali did not increase macrolide resistance in treated children or untreated contacts and met the predefined noninferiority margin in tested isolates. Quarterly administration, however, cannot exclude a modest dose-dependent increase of macrolide resistance in S. pneumoniae and E. coli.

Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0362626
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43024596



Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare soft palate (SP) length, thickness, and volume in French bulldogs and English bulldogs before and after staphylectomy or folded flap palatoplasty (FFP), and to compare the success of procedures in reducing these dimensions. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Dogs diagnosed with brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome (BOAS) underwent staphylectomy (n = 8) or FFP (n = 8). Pre-operative and 4-week post-operative computed tomography was performed to assess SP dimensions and evaluate surgical outcomes. RESULTS: Both procedures resulted in a reduction of SP length (staphylectomy mean reduction = 0.91 cm, 95% CI [0.44 cm, 1.39 cm]; FFP mean reduction = 0.86 cm, 95% CI [0.39 cm, 1.33 cm]), and volume (staphylectomy mean reduction = 2.81 cm3, 95% CI [1.36 cm3, 4.27 cm3]; FFP mean reduction = 2.54 cm3, 95% CI [0.84 cm3, 4.24 cm3]) when comparing pre- and post-operative dimensions within each procedure group. Staphylectomy did not result in SP thinning, while FFP resulted in a mean thinning of 0.30 cm (95% CI [0.10 cm, 0.50 cm]). There was no difference in the degree of SP shortening (adjusted mean difference 0.01 cm, 95% CI [-0.33 cm, 0.35] cm) or reduction of SP volume (adjusted mean difference 0.32 cm3, 95% CI [-0.52 cm3, 1.16 cm3]) between procedure groups. Folded flap palatoplasty resulted in greater SP thinning than staphylectomy. CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: Both staphylectomy and FFP resulted in a reduction of length and volume of the SP. FFP resulted in SP thinning, while staphylectomy did not. In dogs with concurrent SP thickening and elongation, FFP may be the preferred surgical treatment.

Authors: Bajaj S, Quarles CC, Gilmore K, Qiao Y, Wintermark M, Wefel JS, Noll KR, Mokashi C, Zalles M, Roth M
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0360924
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43024577



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Head and neck (HN) cancer survivorship is associated with persistent symptom burden and long-term brain-behavioral health alterations, yet mechanisms underlying brain aging remain poorly understood. We investigated whether HN cancer survivors exhibit accelerated brain aging, whether limbic white matter (WM) pathways contribute to these changes, and whether measures associated with glymphatic function are associated with reduced brain aging. METHODS: Diffusion MRI and symptom burden data were analyzed in 135 HN cancer survivors and compared with a normative cohort from the Human Connectome Project (n = 1,228). Two machine learning models (elastic net [ENET] and random forest [RF]) using fractional anisotropy (FA) and quantitative anisotropy (QA) from 45 WM tracts were trained to estimate brain age and compute brain age gap (BAG). Glymphatic-related processes were indirectly assessed using diffusion tensor imaging analysis along the perivascular spaces (DTI-ALPS). Moderation analyses examined whether symptom burden influenced associations among DTI-ALPS, BAG, and WM integrity. RESULTS: Survivors showed a negative mean BAG of -1.64 years in the ENET model, indicating a nonsignificant tendency toward delayed brain aging, whereas the RF model showed a positive mean BAG of 3.59 years, indicating accelerated brain aging. The RF model demonstrated stronger external generalizability and greater biological coherence, including associations with ALPS and symptom-related measures. The bilateral fornix and right U-fibers were among the strongest contributors to RF-based brain age prediction. Higher DTI-ALPS index values were associated with lower BAG and greater fornix integrity, particularly in survivors with lower symptom burden and reduced activity-related interference. CONCLUSIONS: HN cancer survivorship was associated with accelerated brain aging in the model demonstrating greater external generalizability and biological relevance, alongside alterations in limbic WM pathways. Higher DTI-ALPS was associated with reduced brain aging, with symptom burden modifying this relationship. These findings highlight brain health as an important component of cancer survivorship.

Authors: Elis-Williams L, McDowall F, Harrison C, Hughes K, Crawford A, MacKay JRD
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0362316
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43024576



Abstract:
The welfare of companion animals is predicated by caregiver management and decision making, and so the veterinary consult is a key intervention point to improve animal welfare. As with many health-related behaviours, instigating long-term changes is a challenge in the veterinary profession, with knowledge-deficit models of human behaviour change proving ineffective at promoting positive welfare for companion animals. Dental care is one of the most prevalent health disorders in the UK, with many pets receiving suboptimal Home Oral Hygiene (HOH) care. This study implemented a Dental Care clinic in the Royal (Dick) School of Veterinary Studies Small Animal General Practice and recruited 61 caregivers to a retention-based study looking at changes to HOH. The Dental Clinic followed the 5As framework, adapted for veterinary use, to promote clinically relevant HOH behavioural changes. Caregivers were surveyed prior to the clinic consult, after the final follow-up consult, and at a six month retention date to explore their HOH. Retention was a challenge in the project, with only 39 caregivers attending the clinic, 21 (54%) responding to the End of Clinic survey and 13 (33%) responding to the six month post survey. HOH methods were rated on a 9 point scale, and in the End of Clinic Survey, HOH score had improved by 2.62 points (t student = 2.77, p = .01, g Hedges = 0.58, 95% CI[0.13,1.02]), however, the study was underpowered to detect significance at the Retention stage (FFisher(1.64, 19.63) = 3.28, p = .07, ω^2 p = 0.08, 95%CI[0.00, 1.00]). We discuss the applicability of the 5As framework in veterinary behaviour change, and implications for practice.
